steps.title: Eligibility
out: Epic or story ready to design (and all its stories), entries ready, criteria valid, no design in progress on any
Status of the epic or story: in design
Status of each entry: in design

steps.title: Direction
in: Entry 1: the epic or story, its need entries, intents and criteria
Entry 2: the technical need, in their words
Entry 2, if applicable: the drift spotted by monitoring
out: Direction: constraints, preferences, leads, or the explicit statement "no direction". Human T writes it themselves, no default. Entry 2: adds what must remain true after the change

steps.title: Auditor
steps.actor: AI: a single auditor, who holds the discussion with the human
in: Overview and guidelines, plus the ADRs whose scope overlaps the need's. Selected by script, index first
out: Delta: overlaps, contradicts, hole, code areas touched, estimated extra cost.
Proposed technical scope for each ticket (story or task). The functional scope comes from the need entry

steps.title: Challenge
steps.actor: Human T, opened by script only if the delta is not empty or the extra cost exceeds the threshold
in: The delta, short and in fixed form
On request: a question to the auditor about a line of the delta
out: Revised direction, back to the audit
If extra cost or impossible criterion: card with costed options for human F, entry at status to reframe
The auditor's answer, read-only, quoting the entry concerned. It modifies no document: only a revised intent has an effect

steps.title: Writer
in: In later rounds: human T's answer, or their feedback from the gate
out: Local ADRs, status proposed, with their scope. Entry 2: also carries the why of the need, lacking a wiki entry
Entry 2 only: technical criteria carried by the tickets (non-regression, verifiable invariant)
Proposed split: each story as is, or split into tasks only if necessary. For each ticket: criteria, linked decisions, dependencies, scope
Hypotheses made: each point where it chose a default value (a technical choice, a split, a scope), with the question it would have asked and its default value. It continues with that value
Only if a point blocks it: see the next step

steps.title: Writer's question
steps.actor: Human T, only if the writer is blocked: answers its question
in: Card: the blocking point, the options, the writer's recommendation
out: Answer, back to the writer: it resumes

steps.title: Validator
steps.actor: Persona distinct from the lead: it receives the deliverable alone, never the discussion

agents.when: entry 1: the criteria are covered, the need is not distorted
entry 2: the ADRs are applicable, the tasks autonomous

in: Entry 2: the technical need and its why
out: List of defects, free critique. Entry 1: are the criteria covered, is the need distorted? Entry 2: are the ADRs applicable, the tasks autonomous?

steps.title: Code checks
in: Code structure, to measure the reading size of each task
out: Valid schema, scopes from the vocabulary, each criterion (of each entry of the story, or carried by the task) in exactly one ticket, the story or one of its tasks, dependencies without cycle, cited ADRs exist, no scope overlap with an accepted ADR without "replaces". Direction present, or "no direction" declared by human T. Each criterion linked to at least one decision. Each task carries at least one verifiable criterion. Two tasks with overlapping scopes are linked by a dependency. The reading size of each task (scope, ADR, criteria) fits under the project threshold. A story is split only if it exceeds this threshold

steps.title: Judge

questions.q: Does a local ADR contradict a criterion?
Does the decision linked to a criterion really cover it?

out: Yes or no: does a local ADR contradict a criterion? does the decision linked to a criterion really cover it? Entry 2: does a visible behavior change? If so, switch to the Need workflow

steps.title: Gate · Review
in: Hypotheses made by the writer, with their default value
Code checks and judge, all green
out: ADRs at status accepted, tickets and scopes validated, tickets created at status ready
Or back to the writer if wording, split or a hypothesis must be corrected, or to the direction if the substance

steps.title: Designed
out: An unsplit story is built as is. Otherwise its tasks, thin sub-issues: criteria, decisions, dependencies, scope
Entry 1 only: an unsplit story moves to ready, for the Build. A split story moves to designed, and its tasks are ready. The epic moves to designed when all its stories are. Statuses derived by script
Entry 1 only: status designed for each entry of the epic or story

contract: Entry 1: an epic or a story at status "ready to design" (Need workflow). A story groups one or more wiki entries that go together; an epic groups stories. Entry 2: a technical need expressed directly by human T (debt, migration, remediation, drift fix), a report qualified "technical defect", or the catch-up of a provisional express decision, without a wiki entry.
Accepted local ADRs and ready tickets: each story as is, or its tasks if it was split. For entry 1, the epic or story and its entries move to status designed.
Human T. Human F is consulted only if a criterion is impossible or too costly, or if a technical need changes a visible behavior.
notes: When the challenge opens

A script opens it only if the auditor's delta is not empty. Otherwise writing follows directly. The discussion is a loop between the human and the auditor, with no maximum number of rounds: at each round, the auditor receives the delta and the messages exchanged since its last round.
What blocks the writer

A point is blocking when a choice is covered by no decision or guideline, and its options differ in effect or cost. The writer then asks a question, with the options and its recommendation. Everything else becomes a hypothesis made, visible at the gate.
The writer proceeds, the human decides at the gate

Without a block, the writer continues and the checks chain. Human T is asked before the gate only if a point blocks the writer. At the gate, they can send everything back to the writer. No maximum number of rounds.
Epic, story, task

Human F decides in Need which entries go together (a story) and which stories group (an epic). Plan takes an already-formed epic or story, and does not re-split it functionally. It creates tasks only if the story does not fit as is. A single gate validates the whole.
When to split a story into tasks

A task must be verifiable alone, mergeable alone and fit in one working context. It is not a matter of effort, and a script measures it: at least one criterion per task, a dependency between overlapping scopes, a reading size under the threshold. If the story already meets these three conditions, it is built as is. If it cannot be split without breaking functional meaning, that is a question to human F, who can split the story in Need.
Mandatory direction, no default
The step is not skipped: human T gives a direction, or states themselves that none is needed. Silence does not mean "no direction".
Local ADRs only here
The technical frame produces only guidelines. A local ADR is born in this design, for a story or an epic, or for a technical need.
One validator per entry

The PM validates entry 1, the only one with a functional need to protect. The Dev validates entry 2: both leads are of the same technical side, and the dev will implement. What the code measures (size, autonomy, criteria coverage) is not asked again of the validator.
The audit reads the code
Unlike the technical frame, splitting and dependencies require seeing where the need touches the code.
Entry 2 without wiki
The local ADR is the trace of the technical need, with its why. No need entry is created, since human T is the source.
Promotion
A repeated local ADR becomes a candidate for the Technical frame workflow, detected by its monitoring.
Verification of a local ADR
It is carried by the tests of its tickets' criteria, unlike a cross-cutting ADR that has its own rule.
The only way back to the functional side
An extra cost or impossible criterion sends the entry back to human F, with the costed options.
doc.lede: A need, functional or technical, is translated into local technical decisions and buildable tickets. Splitting into tasks happens here, only if necessary, because it depends on the code.
doc.eyebrow: Run · plan, functional or technical need
